I wrote the draft, but I couldn't run `check-house-rules.mjs`. This session only had file read, write and search tools, with no shell or `node`. Please run it yourself before the fact-check:

`node scripts/check-house-rules.mjs drafts/r10/exhibit-017-illegal-gdp.md`

Using search instead of the script, I found no em or en dashes. The only spelled-out number is "one" in the verbatim quote "at any one time". I counted the body by hand at about 460 words, headings included, under the 500 limit. The script's count is the one that matters.

- **Path:** `C:\Users\betan\AppData\Local\Temp\rounding-errors-bench\2026-11-04-017-generations\drafts\r10\exhibit-017-illegal-gdp.md`
- **Title:** "An arbitrary assumption, legally mandated". "Arbitrary" is ONS's word and "legally mandated" is Patterson's.
- **Frontmatter:** same shape as 015, with no `chartNote`, date 2026-10-23, 7 ledger rows with exactly 1 marked as the gap, and the 3 required verdict rows.

**Judgment calls:**
1. **Category:** I used "the assumptions were the data". It describes how the figure was built, not a verdict, so it fits the vocabulary rules. It's a new category line, so someone needs to add it to the category list in CLAUDE.md at build time. I didn't touch that file.
2. **Gap row:** the 2 figures for 2010 sit in 1 row: "£5.6bn / £4,370m" (the freedom of information reply vs today's MNC8 series). The 78% vs 77% comparison appears only in the body, labelled "this site's arithmetic, not ONS's", followed by "ONS does not say the holiday is the whole difference."
3. **2020 fall:** only the numbers appear, as a ledger row (£5,993m / £4,130m), with no cause and no body line. I cut the body line for length, and the chart will show the drop.
4. **Left out:**
   - Everything in the CUT section.
   - The 125-per-year clothing and condom figures, because the currency isn't confirmed.
   - Which clients-per-week figure ONS actually used: I list only "20, 25 and 30".
   - Patterson's £50bn quote (the en dash problem).
   - The "no drugs except cannabis" assumption, the illegally diluted alcohol comparison and the "controversial" self-employment line, all for length. "Controversial" survives only in the Fraud detected verdict.
   - The FOI reply's date, which the brief says still needs confirming on the page.
5. **Attribution:**
   - Abramsky and Drew appear only as the article's authors.
   - Patterson is quoted as his blog.
   - The body says the ESA95 rule was "old" and quotes ONS's "no changes in this area"; it never says ESA 2010 introduced the rule.
   - "Who lied" answers "Nobody. ONS graded its assumptions in print."
   - Wikipedia appears only as where ONS's footnote points, never as a source.
   - The 2014 ONS article is cited via the UN SIAP mirror, and both the source entry and the disclosure say so.

Two smaller points:
- I wrote the formula as `P\*C\*52` in the body so markdown doesn't italicise the C. The quote in the sources entry stays literal.
- Exhibit 016 also carries the date 2026-10-23. That's allowed, since ties sort by exhibit number, and 017 will list first.
